title: Reviewing the result
caption: Verification checks a result against its contract; validation checks it against the goal. This example uses a person for the goal check; appropriate checks can also be automated.

validation.label: 2 · Validation
validation.question: “Am I building the right product?”
validation.goal: Against the goal: everyone celebrates together
validation.why: Right about what was asked, wrong about what was needed
validation.fixLabel: The fix lands in the contract
validation.fix: Checked by: everyone can join, wheelchair access

two-definitions.description: Boehm defines verification as establishing the correspondence between a software product and its specification, and validation as establishing its fitness or worth for its operational mission [1].

his-two-questions.description: “Am I building the product right?” for verification and “Am I building the right product?” for validation [1].

boehm-verifying-and-validating.title: Boehm, Guidelines for Verifying and Validating Software Requirements and Design Specifications (Euro IFIP 79)

where-the-fix-lands.description: a failed verification changes the product; a failed validation can change the requirements themselves [1].

boehm-verifying-and-validating.title: Boehm, Guidelines for Verifying and Validating Software Requirements and Design Specifications (Euro IFIP 79)

software-practice-not-agents.description: NASA words the same pair as “Are we building the product right?”; applying it to work handed to an agent is an inference [1].

two-checks.title: Two checks
two-checks.script: Borrowing two software concepts, we can ask two different questions of a result. Verification checks it against its contract; validation checks whether it serves the goal. Applying those terms to agent work is an analogy.

paintball-passes.title: Paintball passes
paintball-passes.script: The paintball note passes every line of its contract: an activity for 200, within budget, on the right day. And it still fails the goal, because the contract was right about what was asked and wrong about what was needed.

the-human-part.title: The goal check
the-human-part.script: In this example, a person checks the broader goal, not just the task note. Other checks can be automated where that fits. People choose the oversight, and can review the outcome even when they did not intervene during the task.

your-verdict.title: Your verdict
your-verdict.script: So the next time an agent hands you a result that matches its task perfectly, ask yourself which of the two checks you have actually done.
